reviews.author: Tim
reviews.title: Teddy’s Titanic
reviews.text:
Mom and Son (72 & 50).  We have been to every presidential library and most presidential homes/sites.  By far, this was the worst experience.  From beginning to end, it was poorly envisioned, designed, and executed.

1.  The online ticketing that sells out is absurd as we met several people who were turned away after having traveled long distances.  There is no excuse for this and there should be walk up tickets allotted at various times throughout the day.

2.  As many have previously commented, the parking is horrific.  The design of the parking lot with narrow, one way lanes, as well as limited to no disabled parking—not needed for us but commenting for others—is imbecilic.  The entire parking layout and construction needs to be re-done.  The paver stones leading to the entrance are already significantly cracking and chipping, leaving stumble and trip hazards along the way and clearly reveals the cheap materials and poor construction utilized.

3.  Entering the museum, there is an immediate security checkpoint with a single metal detector.  The line backs up outside of the building and people are forced to stand in the wind/weather.  The only restrooms available are AFTER the security checkpoint.  All above exemplifying the ill-conceived and poorly thought of design.

4.  After security, the scan of your tickets and entering the queue for the library itself.  Here, you can choose to obtain the AI wristband that tracks your movements and interactions through the library as well as provides photos and other digital souvenirs emailed to you.  It’s optional and for us, not worthwhile.

5.  The library itself!  An utter failure and disappointment.  Other than a large main hall containing rows of desks with photos and signage to read, the other rooms are terrible failures in an attempt to incorporate AI into the experience and actually serve to slow down the movement through the library and are so poorly executed they cheapen the entire experience.  Think of an Apple Store with all of the desks throughout with iPads and computers on display.  That’s the main hall with the photos and placards.  The other rooms include a small African safari room, another with a shooting gallery (think the Nintendo video game duck hunt and you envision it perfectly).  Another room features a video of Teddy Roosevelt boating down a river as you sit on the most uncomfortable seating possible which, I assume, the designers thought would be entertaining to design the seating to replicate a canoe for you to sit in and cruise with the video.  Just completely horrible!

6.  Last impression:  If you were some of the unfortunate people who traveled long distances for this albatross and didn’t get to tour, you didn’t miss much.  If you are planning to go out of your way to visit, don’t.  If you’re in the area and happen to get tickets, be prepared for disappointment.

7.  To the museum:  You honestly need to redesign and overhaul this terrible experience.  Did anyone bother to visit the other presidential libraries and think to incorporate the successful ideas and exhibits from those into this one?  Did anyone bother to ask the general public for suggestions?  It’s clear and evident the people who crafted this $450M Hindenburg were more focused on appearance than quality—and you failed wholly on both.

reviews.author: Jane Bongo
reviews.text:
The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, which opened July 4, 2026, in Medora, North Dakota, is less a traditional archives building than a landscape museum. Roosevelt’s official papers still live at the Library of Congress and Harvard. What Medora built is a $450 million, privately run campus on a Badlands butte next to Theodore Roosevelt National Park—meant to put visitors inside the country that formed him.

The architecture is the first exhibit. Snøhetta set the 96,000-square-foot building into the hill, capped it with a walkable roof of native prairie grass, and used rammed-earth walls that read like Badlands layers. Renewable systems already produce more electricity than the building uses. A long breezeway frames the canyons. The boardwalk and grounds are free; the Maah Daah Hey Trail crosses the site. Even if you skip the ticketed galleries, the building-in-the-land is worth the stop.

Inside, the permanent show follows Roosevelt’s life in eight chapters: sickly New York boy, Dakota rancher, Rough Rider, president, Amazon explorer, elder statesman. Plan about three and a half hours. There are genuine artifacts—including African-expedition specimens long in storage—plus a lot of immersion: campfire storytelling, decision games, a “Man in the Arena” room, and an AI Roosevelt you can talk to. Kids stay engaged. Adults who prefer quiet cases of objects may find some of the tech overproduced. The tone is admiring, as Medora’s whole TR industry is, but the galleries do not flatten him into a cartoon.

It is not a research library in the National Archives sense, and it is not a substitute for the national park. It is a high-craft, high-tech life story set in the right place. Pair the visit with a drive or hike in the South Unit. The land still explains Roosevelt better than any screen.

reviews.text:
I go to Medora every year and have been watching the library come along with excitement from its initial stages.
I hate to say this, but after finally visiting it, I was disappointed.

First, entrance is paced so you need to buy tickets for a particular time slot. This should be more widely advertised so people can plan appropriately.

Secondly, many of the exhibits, and when I say that I mean whole rooms, lacked any depth of information. Most items did not state if they were Roosevelt's or not, leading me to believe they were not. The campfire room, while visually cool, did nothing but give a few surface level stories from his life.

Thirdly, the main hall is not easy to navigate and view because of the lines of people waiting to take their AI generated historical selfies. While I understand these are fun, I think less of them and more history would have been better.

Lastly, the gift shop area had little to nothing to do with Roosevelt. Cheap tourist junk. Not a single one of the books he wrote was avaliable.

Here are the things I will recommend: Visit the TR show at the old town hall theater. The entertaining show does a great job of bringing Teddy to life. If you want to read a book written by Teddy, learn more about him, the west, Medora, and many other topics, visit Western Edge Books in town.

reviews.author: Gibson Girl
reviews.text:
As a public historian and museum professional, I was surprisingly disappointed with the TRPL, finding that it had far more in common with a McDonald's Playland than a proper museum or presidential library.

For starters, the prominent display of donor/sponsor names in every single gallery—not to mention right outside on the name of the facility itself, in letter almost as large as Theodore Roosevelt's name—gives the overall impression that this place is less about a proper tribute to our 26th president, and more about an excuse for a handful of wealthy-but-bored benefactors to build a monument to themselves. I completely understand that naming rights are a sad reality in this day and age of philanthropic fundraising, but the effect here was just tacky.

As for the exhibits themselves, they were clearly slapped together very quickly in the end, with some of the sponsor/donor names not even being straight on the wall, many engraved brass artifact labels missing letters or entire words, no maps or handouts to help you find your way through, and no clear signage for where to go. To say nothing of the AI, which bombards you the moment you enter the ticket line and never lets up. Children and even adults were scampering back and forth in every gallery, paying no attention to the history being shared, just eager to see themselves in the next AI-generated picture display. Most of the exhibits were just video stories: sit here and watch video, sit there and listen to a recording. The narrative of Roosevelt's life was also grossly uneven: while understandably emphasizing the two short years TR spent in North Dakota as a young man throughout multiple exhibits, it squeezes the other 58 years of his life into very short soundbytes (for example: a great deal is made of his brief marriage to his first wife, but almost nothing is said about his second wife, the First Lady and mother of most of his children!).

Then there were the accessibility issues. I noted multiple walking-surface changes with no clearly marked transitions; several digital exhibits where you are required to sit on a bench or stool, but with no armrests or mobility assistance nearby; dark galleries, small fonts on the labels, and zero Braille to accommodate visually-impaired visitors; and loud, flashy, in-your-face panoramic-style exhibits without any sensitivity warnings.

Chatting with another family afterward in the gift shop, I asked the kids (elementary school age) what they had learned about Theodore Roosevelt. Their answer? "I don't know, but I was in a lot of pictures." I sincerely hope that was not the intended outcome of the library's builders! And if it were, then I'm even more afraid for the future of the history and museum professions.

The overall impression was that, if you're in the area, have kids, and have several hours to kill, maybe put this on your list of options to entertain them for a few hours. Otherwise you'd be better off saving your money and time, staying home, and reading the David McCullough or Edmund Morris biographies—heck, even his Wikipedia profile will teach you more about TR than this presidential library does.

reviews.text:
It made me so sad. I had such high hopes since the building itself was built with real thought and consideration for the land and the future. Unfortunately, the exhibits are so riddled with generative AI that it was like walking through a psychological haunted house. A museum is no place for cutting creative corners and the presence of AI in that way immediately negates any historical integrity they had. I immediately distrust any pictures or documents because I’m analyzing whether it’s been altered. They animate photos with AI, and however minor that seems, it is a slippery slope to rewriting history. In a federal, educational place like this, that is absolutely terrifying.

I’ve seen Medora use AI for the past couple years, especially regarding Teddy, and it is just gross to me. Maybe there is something I’m missing, but the more research I do on generative AI the more sinister it feels, no matter what “good” it’s used for. Real art is not something that can be optimized and automated.

I gave two stars because the building and grounds are gorgeous, and the food was good. I used to be proud of the way ND embraced TR’s more progressive policies, but walking through the museum made obvious the hypocrisy of idolizing him while voting against everything he stood for. So overall, the museum just made me sad.

This is a great library but I'm not sure that they have the right "flow" of people. Perhaps it's because it's still fairly new. About the first hour is spent waiting in line, first to get in at your designated time, then to show your ticket, next to activate your wristband to enjoy the interactive parts of the library. That part was very slow because many people didn't understand it or required assistance that wasn't available.
Then, this large group of people that just waited in line descends on each exhibit. I gave up trying to get close enough to read- too many people in the way. I would also have appreciated some separate " lanes" for handicapped visitors. There were so many walkers and wheelchairs that made getting around even more difficult.

reviews.title: Innovative, Entertaining, but needs better crowd control!!!!
reviews.text: We had a group of 10 visit this museum in August. We pre-purchased timed admission tickets for 12pm assuming it would help with crowd control since it had oy been open 6 weeks. The crowd was INSANE! We were elbow to elbow with a bazillion other people who were all fighting to maintain spots in line to try and enjoy each museum exhibit. You physically could not stop and read or interact with each station without someone pushing you or in front of you to see for themselves. It was a sad, aggressive, territorial scavenger hunt to try & protect your bubble to try and learn something. They need to do some sort of actual enforced timed, counted entry into each room to help alleviate the horrfic congestion during busy season, especially at the beginning of your experience. Towards the end of the afternoon, the crowd thinned out significantly, and we were able to retrace our steps and actually learn something. The interactive exhibits were innovative and entertaining for all ages in our group, which spanned 3 years old to 70. The Cafe stops serving early, which was a bummer because we spent so much time there due to crowds. Staff are not overly friendly or helpful. It's a beautiful, innovative, shiney new facility. We'd go back, just not in peak season.

reviews.title: Take the whole day - hope it's one of the best museums ever for you too!
reviews.text:
Our trip to the Badlands (ND and SD) was driven by 2 things - the new Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library and the Sturgis Mustang Rally (the later of which drove the timing). 

I am a big US Presidential history geek and thankfully my husband doesn't mind joining me on our various adventures to such libraries. 

We became members of the Library before coming, an investment we will likely continue based on our impressive experience. 

HIGHLY recommend getting timed entry tours and any specialty tour tickets before you arrive. Also recommend allowing time (weather permitting) for exploring the grounds and the museum's rooftop prairie.

We kicked our day off with a guided highlights tour pre-booked. It was a perfect lay of the landscape overview for the intensive, immersive Museum experience.

I deeply appreciate how transparent this facility is in identifying what is an authentic, original artifact and what is a replica. History geek coming out, I know. 

We shared an entree in their Native American themed on site restaurant, Salt & Scoria. Tasty! FYI, their kiosks have a more extensive and complete menu than the beautifully hand written menu that hangs in the restaurant.

Our timed entry tickets followed 1.5 hours after our guided highlights tour, which was just enough time to grab a little lunch before going in. The Museum is well-equipped with staff to help you setup your virtual experiences and get properly checked in. The sold out day we joined (a Saturday) made for shoulder to shoulder experiences - crowded - but almost all kind and considerate humans, thankfully. 

I'd recommend any fellow history geek allow for at LEAST 4 hours for the main museum exhibits and attractions. 

We also added on a late afternoon TR Deep Dive tour. While there was little content overlap between the two tours, our guide for the latter tour was less prepared/more nervous. He might have been new, in fairness - the museum just opened in July and our first guide has been closely involved with the Museum for 5+ years.

This museum is immersive, intensive, beautiful and wonderfully fact focused. Could not recommend the trip any higher!

reviews.author: Majid Shafiei
reviews.text: Great design, poor construction. The design is inspires anyone that visits. However, 3 observations raise concern of shoddy execution or rushed completion. 1) Wood boards and wooden skin panels that were already lifting out of plane due to poor fastening, some showing recent repair attempts with mismatched screws. 2) rammed earth wall with extensive vertical cracking through multiple lifts, and crumbling sections along the bottom of lifts. I suspect this is due to uneven mixing (crumbling) or overly tight fastening to the underlying support structures which expand and settle at a different rate than the wall. 3) poured concrete floor at entrance to lobby with long cracks diagonally across the slab rather than in the joints. I'm no construction expert, but I encourage building professionals to take a look. It would be a shame if such an impressive design, with the power to revolutionize design in the US, were to become the example used to reinforce the unimaginative and unsustainable status quo.

reviews.author: Michelle Rigby
reviews.text: What a treasure to all who visit! The process was very easy. We ordered tickets with a specific time slot online. When we showed up, we went through security and showed our online tickets from phone. We received an arm bracelet which you then register at the kiosk so you can participate in the interactive displays throughout the library. The timeline of Theodore Roosevelt’s life is laid out for visitors. We were impressed with the diversity of the displays and how you could interact with them. There is plenty of seating to take a rest as you need to. The outside of the library is unlike anything I have seen before. The roof is completely covered with landscape. The architects did a phenomenal job of making the library part of the landscape of the badlands. There is also walking trails (in full sun). Plenty of seating outside that was covered along with some of the parking. I highly recommend a visit to the new presidential library.

What’s so cool about this place is that it was made for all ages to enjoy even though we hear that all of the time we were with a party that had five generations in it and there is something for everyone even our eight-year-old grandson enjoyed it, and never once said he was bored that in itself is amazing!  Another stunning feature of this location is that the architecture was created to blend in with the Badlands of North Dakota truly a one-of-a-kind. It was also designed with some very special features in mind like the way it was positioned so that the snow does not go through the breezeways where the entries are and the wood is especially treated wood that will not deteriorate anytime soon in the harsh weather of the Dakota’s. I found it especially interesting to speak directly to Theodore Roosevelt in his office as an AI and I did ask him several questions. This presidential library features such a unique interactive experience that we ended up spending about four hours there, but with all the information and nostalgic items and collectibles that are presented, you could actually spend two days there just absorbing all of the information and knowledge. The location has great parking and it also features a deli style restaurant. The open area is feature a grand view of the Badlands. This was a unique and cultural experience, and it gives me additional profound respect our great country, what all of us have been through in historical times up to today is eye opening. All Americans should experience this and put it on their bucket list. Enjoy!😊

reviews.author: Damon Horn
reviews.text:
The location is absolutely beautiful and the architecture is breathtaking. The trails are a very pleasant and the site was clearly set up with care. The exhibits are engaging and use technology well. I only have 2 complaints:

1) It took around 30-40 minutes to get in. The line was moving very slowly because the digital check in kiosks took a while.

2) I asked the AI Teddy Roosevelt a question ("Did you support Eugene Debs imprisonment for protesting the draft?") The computer had to think for a long time, then basically said that while he disagreed with Debs, freedom of speech is important and he should have the right to say what he wants. I researched the exact question later and found that TR had said many negative things specifically about Debs and had written in support of jailing people for opposing WWI and the draft. It was disappointing to have received inaccurate information in the library, and a reminder that AI can be tricky and overconfident. I wish the AI exhibit had simply said it didn't know the answer instead of making something up that didn't fit the facts.

Alternatively you could have a docent or TR impersonator answer questions, which I have seen work well at other museums.

Despite these two quibbles, the museum is overall excellent and I enjoyed myself.

reviews.text: Hit up several presidential libraries on my travels--Lincoln, Reagan, Nixon--and never once needed a timed ticket. Just showed up and went in. Then I drove way out to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in the middle of North Dakota, and they turned me away at the door because I didn't have a reservation. reviews.author: Benjamin
reviews.title: If You’re Looking for North Dakota Hospitality, This Ain’t It.
reviews.text: I’ve visited several presidential libraries across the country, including Lincoln in Springfield, Reagan in Simi Valley, and Nixon in Yorba Linda. None of them required timed tickets—you could simply walk in. So I drove hours out of my way to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota, only to be turned away at the door because I didn’t have a reservation. I explained the long drive and asked if there was any way to accommodate us, but the staff member seemed almost offended by the request and offered no sympathy or flexibility whatsoever. At twenty-six dollars a ticket and with the place clearly not crowded, that kind of attitude feels completely out of place for a destination this remote.

reviews.text: Really a fantastic place. Our only complaint is that we couldn't see every detail due to the crowds. Get your tickets in advance and choose a morning time if possible. I loved the movie about Teddy's trip in the amazon. The interactive exhibits which allow you to insert your photo into the scene were amazing. Everything about the library is amazing. Well done, bravo! We especially loved seeing Teddy's authentic diary on display in a carefully lit room -- opened to the page where he wrote a huge X after the death of his mother and beloved wife on the same day. There is so much to see and do in this venue. If I could do it again, I would visit on two separate days, with hikes in-between. It's a four-hour venue but the human body is just built for two-hour max museum visits. So .... when planning your trip ... worth it to plan for two visits.

reviews.author: Brian O'Connor
reviews.text:
Ticket system is clunky. They need to hold back more tickets for each time block so people can walk up and get tickets the day of. Especially considering its in a location of the country that most people are only passing through maybe once in their life. We had to change our travel plans because of the ticket system.

The library itself is an AI data gathering center surrounded by a few boards of information about Teddy Roosevelt. They ask for your personal information and only tell you its to add to your experience while going through the exhibits. I asked several times what this meant and the guy refused to answer my question and got very frustrated with me for wanting to know.

After going through the library its 100% unnecessary to give your info for the AI slop in the exhibits (imo). It seems the library was designed for young kids and people with very short attention spans. The use of AI generated self portraits felt like just a cute distraction and was in no way a meaningful part of learning about Teddy. The gift shop or lobby would have been a better place for those stations. It would have lessened the crowds just standing and taking up space.

Most of the AI stuff interferes with people who are actually trying to read the information panels. At one point I was tying to read while people walked in front of me that were only there doing an AI scavenger hunt with their wrist bands that made loud bird calls in the room we were in. That was very distracting and frustrating to my experience.

The other AI stations offered very little in terms of adding depth to the museum. All in all this is a pretty sad representation of Teddy Roosevelt and the things he advocated for.

The library feels like a "must stop" thing to see given its location but lacks a lot of substance.

reviews.author: Elliot Bishop
reviews.text:
I never thought a presidential library would remind me of Disneyland, but this one does, and not in the good ways.
Pros:
The building and grounds are beautiful, and are worth visiting on their own, which is free.
Narration by Nick Offerman, I can’t think of a better person for the job.
The exhibit does a good job of connecting the past to the present and future at the end.

Cons:
Overcrowded – despite timed entry they are still letting too many people in. You will still have to wait in line to get in (and once inside), which is slow partially due to the optional photo and information entry for the “enhanced experience”.
Too much reliance on technology. All of the tap points make it feel more like a theme park than a museum. Lines form around the stations where you can get your face on an old time photo. The multi-projector video rooms are unnecessarily overwhelming with visuals where a simple well-done video would have been fine. The use of technology is so aggressive it feels uncomfortable against the historical subject matter, especially considering the conservation themes.
I did not expect a new museum to have many original artifacts, and in fact there are a lot of replicas.

It is worth a visit if you need to distract your kids with something (there is a literal playground type fort inside). I would not recommend it to anyone who appreciates traditional museums/history centers/visitor centers where you can meander, read, and observe.

I wish I would've had more time. It's new as it just opened a month ago so obviously it was very very busy . I love to see everyone so excited about history. I don't know when I'll ever get back to Medora again, but this was probably the highlight of the trip.

I went with some of my nieces And it was really fun viewing the museum through their eyes. Particularly the interactive room with TR where you can ask him all sorts of questions that was just so educational. I can see why this museum took so long to come to fruition. But it's absolutely superb.

reviews.title: It’s more than a library
reviews.text: Definitely a unique and fun experience. Once inside, the fresh wood furniture smell is evident. We got bracelets as part of the experience for interactive exploring. Make sure you use it to tap the many photo ops and seek and find animals to log your own personal online journal. Once you take your photo at the beginning, it’s used to create these Theodore Roosevelt period, black and white portraits. Pretty cool. Each exhibit is educational and entertaining. Lots to see and take in. Very awe inspiring and showcased Roosevelt’s accomplishments and contributions to America’s greatness. He had so many inspiring quotes that were used throughout the library. It took us 3 hours easily and we don’t think we covered all. Must visit before it gets too popular. It got very crowded as people came and stayed. Food wasn’t great, maybe they will improve. Souvenirs were pricey even for a postcard. Surrounding canyon sights were magnificent. Glad we drove 4 hours from Mt Rushmore to get there.

reviews.author: Abby H
reviews.title: First Time Visitor
reviews.text: Wow! What an experience. I was gifted tickets without any prior knowledge of what to expect. I have visited many museums, and this by far, exceeded my expectations. The interactive exhibits made it engaging for young children and an incredible educational experience. In no time, three hours had escaped us. If you have mobility issues, I highly recommend being dropped off at the front entrance and riding the golf cart to the front door. Most likely, there will be a line to stand in even if you have purchased tickets ahead of time. Once you make it through the first exhibit, there is adequate seating options to rest at before venturing to other exhibits. Try to bring as little as possible so your hands won’t be tied up and you can easily access the interactive exhibits. There are clean restrooms available upon walking in and within the main area. reviews.title: Wonderful trip to Theodore Roosevelt library
reviews.text:
The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota, is one of the state's premier attractions and sits on a bluff overlooking Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

The exhibits tell Theodore Roosevelt's life story, from a rancher in the Badlands to the 26th U.S. president.

reviews.title: Educational experience but they’re still working on some issues.
reviews.text: The library is beautiful. The problem is getting to the library because the signage is so poorly done. Our friend requires a handicap parking space for which there was absolutely zero signs to indicate how to get there. We asked one of the employees where those parking spaces were and she said that the pavement is marked, but when people parked over them, no one else even realizes that they are there. Once you park, it is still quite a hike to get up to the entrance to the library. I only saw one or two shuttles that were available to take people who needed additional assistance to get from the limited parking area up to the entrance. After you get to the entrance you get in a line and wait to be sent through a freestanding scanner. The scanner later blew over & broke when a wind storm blew through. Once you’re cleared to go in, there’s another line to get in to go through to get your ticket scanned. Then you’re given the opportunity to sign up with your wristband to be able to take pictures of yourself throughout the library. If you decide to go, I recommend planning a full day in order to stop and read every single display that they have. It’s very interesting & educational but it’s also very time-consuming and daunting, especially if there’s large crowds. The observation of the four of us in our group decided that we much more enjoyed the Bush library we have been through in Texas.
reviews.response_text:
Thank you for a detailed and useful review. On the accessible parking, you're right and it's a design failure rather than bad luck - markings painted on the pavement are no use once a vehicle is on top of them. Better signage is a priority fix.

On the shuttles: those golf carts run from the drop-off circle for anyone who needs them, and your friend shouldn't have had to make that walk. The fact you saw only one or two and read it as scarcity tells us we aren't making the service visible enough, which is on us. Ask any Welcome team member, or call ahead on 701-892-6070. More at trlibrary.com/visit/accessibility

Thank you also for flagging the scanner. That has gone to the operations team.

- The team at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

reviews.text:
This is a well constructed museum experience, though I don't know enough to know if it constitutes a "Presidential Library". Some of the experiences and moments of Theodore Roosevelt's life are very well orchestrated, such as the presentation of his tragic loss and the diary entry after. Some of the experiences felt less than they could have been with the computer generated/AI elements. I did not interact with the AI Teddy because it feels hollow and not worth the time, with all the other moments being more impactful.

There is some sad irony in the trust-busting and monopoly-fighting that TR did alongside the nature of how this place came together, as well as the current push to take, end, or sell public lands to the highest bidders which Teddy probably would be turning in his grave over.

The (literal) windows to the Badlands sprinkled throughout  the walking experience were well architected and planned.  The walk along the roof and the building melding into the Badlands is well done.

reviews.author: Obaidullah Rahim
reviews.text:
The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library exceeded every expectation. This is far more than a library - it’s an unforgettable experience that perfectly blends history, architecture, technology, and the breathtaking beauty of the North Dakota Badlands. Every exhibit is immersive, thoughtfully designed, and engaging for visitors of all ages. You don’t just learn about Theodore Roosevelt’s life - you feel connected to his journey and the values that shaped him.

The building itself is a masterpiece, seamlessly blending into the surrounding landscape, and the panoramic views alone are worth the visit. The interactive exhibits kept us engaged for hours, and the staff was welcoming, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about sharing Roosevelt’s legacy.

If you’re anywhere near Medora or Theodore Roosevelt National Park, this is an absolute must-see. I came away inspired, educated, and with an even greater appreciation for conservation, leadership, and American history. Without a doubt, one of the best museums and historical attractions I’ve ever visited.

Amazing place!!! My very active 11,9&6 year old boys really liked it and never were bored (just hungry at the end) for 2.5 hours. Walk the roof and the grounds in the morning before the summer noon temperatures. Inside, the kids can find hidden animals in about seven of the rooms while the adults read all the materials in the room (and the adults can look for the animals too). In the middle is the White House gang, which is very fun information but is actually a play area for kids with rubber building blocks and rope bridges. A little ways before that there is digital cow hearding and an electric shooting game that four people can play -- this is in the area you learn about TR as a cowboy. Follow the map of the museum and use your wrist band at the progress check kiosks to make sure you haven't missed anything. You also get to see yourself in seven different scenes, make an election poster and campaign for yourself, and a fee other activities-- ALL of which are emailed to the email you provided at check in when you get your wristband and take your photo before the tour.
So much to see, my wife and I will definitely be back to see what all we missed.

reviews.text: I have visited many museums, including presidential museums all over the country, and this one is the most amazing museum I have ever visited! The details integrated with technology made it interactive, educational, and fun.  Adults and kids will love putting themselves into history while they learn about the life and times of Theodore Roosevelt. The construction of the museum was also well done. The design of the walls mimicking the layers of soil in the surrounding area to the large windows showing the exterior landscape showcases the thoughtful design. The building feels like it belongs in the landscape. It is 100% worth the drive to see. My kids are already asking when we can return!

reviews.author: Vish Birbal
reviews.text: Though more like a museum than a library, this was a fantastic experience! My wife and I loved the AI photos they made of us as well as the really cool mini-theaters detailing TR's Rough Riders and Brazilian river expedition. The AI conversation with the hologram was a bit glitchy but a cool concept overall.

reviews.author: Maria Aimen J.
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, we were not able to even visit the library, because, apparently, you had to buy tickets in advance. 
We had parked our car, and went through security, then come to find out that you need to buy tickets to visit a library. I had no idea, no libraries near us do that. Nor do any libraries I've ever been to. Apparently all of the reviews that I read online did not mention that you had to purchase a ticket. I asked, how much it was, and one of the security girls had to ask the other one, who said it was $26 (check online if you want to confirm). I figured since we already drove up here,  I would buy them,  so I told her that I would be purchasing them for my family, and she said that they already had sold out yesterday. So that was a letdown. 

The outdoor of the library was beautiful. You could tell that everything looks brand new. There were people singing near the rocking chairs, although they were singing pretty explicit things with families around. I'm not sure how it is with those people, but had my parents been with me, like theirs were with them, it would make me really uncomfortable to be with my parents and hear those songs. 
I would have given them five stars even if I wasn't able to go into the library if workers do not have to ask each other how much the price of the tickets are, and those explicit songs. On the plus side, the bathrooms were clean.  They also had a water bottle refill fountain right by the bathrooms.
reviews.response_text:
We're sorry - parking, clearing security and then finding out you couldn't get in is a bad sequence, and the ticketing should have been obvious long before that point. We're working on making it clearer well before anyone leaves home.  Summer is a busy season for Medora and anyone looking to visit from June-September we highly recommend booking in advance online.

The singing near the rocking chairs shouldn't have happened with families around, and thank you for telling us. That's gone to the grounds team.

You also shouldn't have had to wait while two staff worked out the admission price. That's a training gap and a fair thing to be annoyed about.

Thank you for the note about the restrooms and the water refill station. Small things, easy to get wrong.

- The team at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

reviews.text:

It's the most sustainable presidential library ever built and one of the most regenerative cultural buildings in the Americas.

The library is a source of inspiration - for all!

reviews.author: Stewart King
reviews.text: An amazing museum with a comprehensive portrait of the man and his times. They did a good job of presenting the complexity and historical context. The exhibits were interesting, though they didn't actually have a lot of Roosevelt items; most of the documents and items they present are replicas of items that you can see in the original at Oyster Bay or (for the documents) at Harvard. I didn't do the interactive features but young people who were using them seemed to be amused; if I was there with kids I would certainly have participated. The architecture and grounds are fantastic! You get a good sense of the place and what it must have felt like to live here more than a century ago. What this is not is a library - Roosevelt's papers are at Harvard and even the tchotchke shop was very light on books. I was actually looking for Darren Lunde's The Naturalist, on Roosevelt's environmental initiatives, and didn't find it. The 25 bucks to get in was somewhat of a surprise but this is a private foundation, not the Park Service or the Archives, so be warned. Nevertheless, I recommend a visit to flesh out your experience in the stunning National Park next door.

You don’t *have* to, but for any of the interactive items, which is basically the entire thing since it’s all based on AI, you need to do it. They claim that your info and image is deleted after 30 days, but not sure I believe that.

Minus 1 star due to how terrible gift shop is, Hardly anything there for souvenirs with the actual “Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library” on it. No magnets, no stickers, slim selection of shirts; very sad we didn’t get our usual tourist magnet and/or sticker for our collections.

Otherwise, the library/museum is informative and showcases his life well, just wish it didn’t rely so heavily on AI. Very surprising that everything isn’t protected from people touching them.

E,

Thank you for visiting.  The Trailblazer and AI photo stations are not required for participants.  While we encourage it you can still enjoy the original TR objects, films, and traditional museum displays.  Most interactives still offer an ability to tap and participate without regsitering.

Thank you for your feedback and we hope you had a safe journey.

reviews.text:
Awesome! Just plain awesome. Know when you go to go through the museum in order, it mimics his life story. I think the premise was to get people to wind through a certain way, but the big gallery room kinda confuses the flow. You will move front to back, and side to side as you progress. I think everyone is just so new they are figuring out things. 

In addition, the restaurant was closed for an event, and the gift shop only had $12 Cokes. There was one water fountain near the restrooms. They really need to rethink the needs of the customers when they are spending 3+ hours in the museum. There is ample outside space to explore, great walking paths, and rocking chairs to enjoy the view (just need more). Parking filled up really fast, I hope they will develop more, and a shuttle from the far lots. 

All in all, this experience is fantastic, it is terrific for kids, take your time, enjoy the story!

reviews.text:
Mixed feelings about it.  I learned a few things. I noticed some of the object labels had text that sounded rather 'woke', not necessarily a quote from TR but rather someone's thoughts on what he said.  A lot of messaging about 'how you should be'.

This is not a museum with 1000's and 1000's of artifacts. Some good tech but generally speaking this place did not exude warmth - instead it was bright, with a lot of tech which came off as cold and many times shallow. It seems out of balance at many points, providing space & over-the-top presentation for something that would be better served up in a simple, direct way. Did I learn more about him, yes. Do I feel more connected to TR, taking pride in him as a man - no. So the info was there but the meaning wasn't.

No printed receipt. You have to provide your email address if you want a receipt. A place this large, with so many attendees does not provide a printed receipt. You can provide your email, plus you can get your photo taken of your face so the AI programs can photoshop you into a different outfit. What do they do with all the facial images they collect from visitors?

It received a lot of hype when Trump was there the week of July 4th, 2026 - but I don't think it lived up to the hype.  I thought it was over priced but if you are going to be in Medora anyways (for the musical) then it is reasonable to go here too. But I wouldn't drive out of my way to see it.

BTW, security wasn't particularly on point.
reviews.response_text:
Thank you — there's a lot here and most of it is actionable.

On the labels: the exhibits present a full life, including the parts that are still argued about. Reasonable people read that differently and we'd rather have the argument than avoid it. If a specific label reads as editorialising rather than history, tell us which one and we'll look at it properly.

On the photographs, the picture you take at the station isn't kept. The period portraits it generates are held for 30 days so you can download them, then permanently deleted. Registration is optional too — decline it and you can still see everything in the building.

The security note and the printed receipt have both gone to the team.

— The team at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

reviews.author: Spokanic
reviews.title: The building steals the show
reviews.text:
An architectural and landscape architectural masterpiece that beautifully complements the Badlands. 

The place is a shrine to TR, and exhibits gloss over some of his shortcomings (racism, imperialism) while underplaying some of his greatest achievements (trust busting, labor rights, land conservation, national parks). The building is all about the conservation ethos while exhibits dwell more on conquering Cuba, playing cowboy, adventuring in the Amazon—the Disney version of TR. But it’s all pretty fun and engaging.
reviews.response_text:
This is the most useful review we've had, we are grateful for your honest critique.

Every topic you name is covered - race, empire, his treatment of Native Americans, trust busting, labor, the public lands. What we can't do is give any of them the room they deserve on an exhibit panel. A wall label holds a few hundred words. Roosevelt's life doesn't. That constraint is real, and it's the thing you're feeling.

Where we can go deeper is trlibrary.com, and that's deliberate. The exhibits are meant to be a starting place rather than the last word - if someone leaves wanting to read more about Roosevelt and his world, that's the design working.

If particular rooms left the impression of a shrine, tell us which ones. Weight and placement we can act on.

- The team at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

reviews.author: Crystal
reviews.text: Absolutely incredible experience. Each exhibit is set up with interactive displays that make the experience incredibly immersive. You become part of the story itself. Yes, AI generation is relied on, heavily, but it's used in a very cool way. As you enter, you are given a compass wrist band and your photo is taken. The wristband becomes your "check-in" device for each exhibit. A log is kept of the exhibits you have attended. Each check-in puts you into a different part of TR's story and AI images are created in your likeness as part of the story. The wristband also activates different AI displays, such as animals moving from a book display onto a screen behind it. Without giving away too much, there is also an exhibit where you can feel actual movement. There are some neat projects on the campaign trail and during the presidential years. The choices you make in these activities come together in the end (my favorite part). The architecture is absolutely stunning and the views are incredible.  The staff was wonderful. The site is ADA compliant, including the rooftop trail. I was also informed that staff are available to assist in pushing wheelchairs (although I'm not certain that is guarantee based on staffing).

This is an amazing place for every age and political view unless you're anti-AI or surveillance state. There are interactive activities tied to a personal token throughout the displays, from creating AI gen items through TRs life, to finding hidden animals through out.

The amount of artifact and history contained is amazing and will require multiple visits. I can see people being concerned regarding the amount of data collected from each visitor,  but it's nothing unique if you have any app on your smart phone. At least here they are connecting it to something educational and creating a unique experience for each individual.

The outside is amazing too, there is a boardwalk providing great views of the library and surroundings, not to mention a walkway on the roof.

The food and gift shop are the areas that could use some work but outside the main purpose of the building.

This is a type of place you go out of your way to go to,  even if it's in rural North Dakota and live on a coast.

reviews.text:
This was a beautiful new library, here are my pros and cons:

Pros:
- Lovely exhibits and easy to walk through Teddy’s whole life. Great tribute to such an important historical figure
- Beautiful outdoor area to explore/cafe with nice options
- Sustainability as a priority with the building being in nature

Cons:
- They do not make it clear that if you get your photo taken before entering for their “interactive journal” that you’re essentially consenting to your face being entered in Google Gemini’s AI model. That felt weird, even if the stops in the museum to “make old timey pictures of yourself” seemed fun.
- Different lines for walk-in tickets and the interactive bracelet. We could have saved 30 minutes by not getting the bracelet for the interactive parts… (if you have the ticket and don’t want the wristband, you can walk directly to the entrance on the left side)

This is the first presidential library that I have visited, and it has set the bar incredibly high for an future presidential library visits!

This library is visually stunning, thoughtfully arranged, and extremely interactive and informative.  I was a little worried about how well our kids (ages 7, 11, and 14) would do at something like this, but we spent between 4-5 hours there without a single complaint.

I'd recommend buying tickets ahead of time to reserve a spot and save a few minutes on your way in.  When you arrive, there is free parking and then you head to the breezeway between the two buildings (library on one side and event and office space on the other).  You'll go through a security point before you enter and they do not allow any guns or knives of any sort in the building so I'd leave them in your car if you have them.

Once you enter you will get a bracelet to wear that has a chip in it that will give you access to all of the interactive parts of the library.  Then you'll register your bracelet with your name, email, and photo and head into the exhibits.  (The photo is for some some of the AI generated images. See pics below. But if you're worried big brother is watching, you can probably skip it if you want, but I'd highly recommend it.  Our kids thought it was awesome and hilarious.) You will get an email with your photos and also other parts of the experience that are a part of your "journal".

The exhibits walk through different phases of TR's life and experiences and lets you join in the experience in almost every area of the library.

TR and his family loved animals, so throughout the museum exhibits are animals you can try and find and scan with your bracelet to collect them all.  Our younger two had fun trying to find them all and it got them excited to travel from room to room.  Our 14 year old enjoyed the different interactive pieces of different exhibits too.

You can also do some walks outside and on the roof of the building!  Very fun and unique experience with incredible views.

If you're in the area, I can't recommend this place enough for you (and your family)! We did the library from 9-1:30, TR National Park from 2-5 (ate picnic lunch in the car), dinner from 5:30-6:30, and the Medora Musical to cap our day.  Great family trip! Hope you have as much fun as we did!

reviews.text:
Tl;dr: For the sake of fairness, I will try to ignore my tremendous bias, as I am an ardent admirer of Theodore Roosevelt (henceforth referred to as TR). That being said, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is an experience unparalleled. “It was here that the romance of my life began” - TR

Service and Price: Memberships at the library cover admission, and regular tickets can be had at different price points for military, students, seniors, and children. All the staff, from the cafe to the janitors to the curators, were second to none! Friendly, passionate, and professional from start to finish.

Experience: Depending on how fast you want to go and how many things you want to do, it will take 2-4 hours to get through the whole exhibit. The first thing you are prompted to do is take a photo at one of their photo stations. Part of the museum experience is interactive, and they take your photo and show you what you would look like if you were part of TR’s entourage throughout significant events of his life, which is tracked via a bracelet given to you at the beginning of the self guided tour. The museum takes you through the life of TR, starting as a child. You journey through his childhood home, his time in the Badlands, his return to politics, his career in government service, and what he did after his career. Each portion of his life is prefaced in the main hall, off which the immersive exhibits all branch. There are numerous items from his life that are on display, and it is all expertly curated. Of course, they do have everything to keep adults engaged, but they also have a good number of activities to keep the kids engaged as well. I would jump at the opportunity to go again, and fully intend to return upon my next journey to Medora.

Location: The TR Presidential Library is located in the North Dakota Badlands, in the town of Medora. It is up a very steep hill, so walking to it would be very difficult, but they share a parking lot with the Medora Musical, so once you get up the hill, parking is plentiful and the walk into and around the building is flat and easy. And for those wondering, Theodore Roosevelt spent a few years ranching around Medora, after his mother and wife passed away on the same day, the latter of whom had just given birth to this daughter. He chose to come to Medora because he appreciated the desolate and haunting beauty of the land, but also the simplicity and honest nature of the work and lifestyle. By his own admission, his experiences here were what helped shape him into the incredible leader he became.

Grounds and Interior: The first thing you see as you crest the hill is how the museum rises gracefully from the earth, while still being part of it like a natural hill. Native plants decorate the rooftop, which you can walk onto via a meandering walking path on one side, and staircase on the other. Another walking path about half a mile long takes you on a large flat loop in front of the museum to showcase some of the quiet beauty the badlands offer.  All parts of the grounds are wheelchair accessible. To enter the museum, you walk through a massive breezeway, which offers rocking chairs and a view overlooking the town below. The whole building extensively includes natural materials throughout, including wood flooring and rammed earth walls. The massive windows really open up the space, and bring the outdoors into your experience.

Overall: As a true Theodore Roosevelt fan, this is as pure of an experience as you can have. You get to experience all of the highs and lows and adventures of TR’s life. It does an excellent job at not only showing you what his life was like, but immersing you into each part of his journey. The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is an absolute must see, even if you are only driving through. Your time will be well rewarded with incredible history at a world class facility.

reviews.author: mrc282
reviews.title: cowboy turn president 1901-1909
reviews.text:
Theodore Roosevelt is a multifaceted figure: soldier, peacemaker, hunter, conservationist, diplomat, opportunist. 

I havent been to many presidential libraries, but this one stands out due to its interactive and AI-powered feature. Despite being the 26th president, his library was just officially completed and inaugurated on 4 July 2026 in conjunction with 250th anniversary of US's independence. 

When you enter, you are first given a wrist band that is linked to your name / email / photo. later, within the museum, you will be able to see yourself depicted as various figures during the TR era and interact with TR (or at least its lifelike representation) by scanning against a compass icon. 

As the museum just opened, entry is enforced by time slot. There is security check but bottled water/camera/mobile phones/small bag are fine. Make sure you book well in advance online if you are on a tight schedule

reviews.text:
3 hours of pure entertainment and education is definitely not enough time to see just the library itself; let alone the the roof, the landscape, and the hiking.
"True" liscenced service animals  have no restrictions here, and you can bring a small dog as long as you can carry your pet or put it in a bag. Then they can come along also which is very similar to the rules of Crazy Horse Memorial /Monument in SD.

reviews.author: Ann Lawton (Ann Lawton)
reviews.text: Amazing library. Opened last weekend. Walk through Tr's life through a state of the art facility. Not just his presidency. So positive. Wow. Special amenities for children. Incredible setting. Staff very helpful. Parking right there. Lots of places to sit. Timed entry. So many folks and descendants worked for years to bring this tribute to life. Set on the top of a hill to view his beloved Badlands. Sit in a rocking chair and enjoy the view, or have lunch in the cafe.

reviews.author: Sawyer Shepherd
reviews.text: Fantastic experience! The entire campus is gorgeous and it’s done in a way that does not detract from the nature around it at all.
